title: Noetherian approximation of a finitely presented algebra and module (Stacks 00R1)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and let $M$ be a finitely presented $S$-module, meaning that $M$ is the cokernel of an $S$-linear map $S^{\oplus a}\to S^{\oplus b}$ for finite $a,b$. Then there are a nonempty directed set $(\Lambda,\le)$, ring maps $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ and $S_\lambda$-modules $M_\lambda$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$, compatible transition maps and maps to $R,S,M$, such that: (1) $R=\varinjlim R_\lambda$, $S=\varinjlim S_\lambda$ as rings and $M=\varinjlim M_\lambda$ as abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], compatibly with $R\to S$ and the module actions; (2) each $R_\lambda$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_\lambda$ is of finite type over $R_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], while $M_\lambda$ is finitely generated over $S_\lambda$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (3) for every $\lambda\le\mu$, the canonical maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$ and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to M_\mu$ are isomorphisms; (4) for every $\lambda$, the canonical maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$ and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to M$ are isomorphisms, so also $M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to M$ is an isomorphism of $R$-modules.
